generic.context: This generic error message appears across the platform when an unexpected system error happens that doesn't have a specific error message. Users encounter this during various operations like saving content, loading data, or API failures when a more detailed error description isn't available.

component.description: A global error handling component that catches unhandled exceptions and displays fallback error messages to users. It prevents the entire application from crashing when unexpected errors occur during normal platform operations.

generic.usage: Error message text displayed in error dialogs, toast notifications, or error boundary fallback screens
generic.impact: Critical - this is the fallback error message users see when system failures occur, requiring clear communication to maintain trust

network.value: Network error. Please check your connection.
network.context: This error message appears when the platform cannot connect to AWS Amplify DataStore, OpenAI services, or other network resources. Users see this message in error notifications, toast messages, or modal dialogs when network connectivity issues prevent data synchronization, AI features, or content loading from functioning properly.

component.description: A global error handling component that displays network connectivity errors across the platform. This component manages error states for AWS Amplify DataStore sync failures, OpenAI API connection issues, and general network connectivity problems that affect learning content delivery.

network.usage: Error notification message displayed in toast notifications or error dialogs when network connectivity fails.
network.impact: Critical - Network connectivity is essential for all platform functionality including content sync, AI features, and real-time collaboration.

invalid_credentials.context: This error message appears when users attempt to log in with incorrect credentials on the authentication screen. It displays after clicking the login button when either the username/email or password doesn't match any valid account in the system.

component.description: The login form component handles user authentication and credential validation. It displays error messages when login attempts fail due to incorrect or non-matching credentials.

invalid_credentials.usage: Error message displayed below the login form after failed authentication attempt
invalid_credentials.impact: High - This is critical feedback that prevents user confusion and guides them to correct their login credentials

session_expired.value: Your session has expired. Please sign in again.
session_expired.context: This error message appears when a user's authentication session has timed out due to inactivity or token expiration. It displays as a notification or alert, typically redirecting users to the sign-in page to re-authenticate before they can continue using the platform.

component.description: Authentication session management component that monitors user session validity and handles token expiration events. It triggers re-authentication flows when sessions expire and manages secure transitions back to authenticated states.

session_expired.usage: Error notification message displayed when session authentication fails
session_expired.impact: Critical - Users must understand they need to sign in again to continue accessing their learning content and progress

required.context: This validation message appears beneath form input fields when users attempt to submit a form without filling in mandatory fields. It displays in red text immediately after the user clicks submit or moves focus away from an empty required field, providing instant feedback about missing information.

component.description: A form validation component that displays error messages for required fields across all forms in the platform. It appears dynamically when form validation fails and provides immediate feedback to users about missing or invalid input data.

required.usage: Error message text that appears below empty required form fields upon validation
required.impact: Critical - prevents users from successfully submitting forms and completing essential actions like registration, content creation, or assignment submission

invalid_email.context: This error message appears when users enter an incorrectly formatted email address in form fields such as registration, login, profile settings, or invitation forms. Users see this validation message immediately after entering an invalid email format or upon form submission when the email validation fails.

component.description: This component displays form validation error messages to provide immediate feedback to users when they enter invalid data. It appears below or adjacent to input fields to guide users in correcting their entries before form submission.

invalid_email.usage: Error message displayed below email input fields when validation fails
invalid_email.impact: Critical - prevents users from completing essential actions like registration and login, directly blocking platform access

password_mismatch.context: This error message appears during user registration or password change flows when the user enters different values in the 'Password' and 'Confirm Password' fields. It displays immediately after the user exits the confirm password field or attempts to submit the form, preventing account creation or password updates until resolved.

component.description: A form validation component that handles password confirmation during user registration and password reset processes. It provides real-time validation feedback to ensure users enter matching passwords before allowing form submission.

password_mismatch.usage: Error message displayed below password confirmation input field or in form validation summary
password_mismatch.impact: Critical - blocks users from completing essential account setup or security updates, directly affecting platform access

upload_failed.context: This error message appears when a user attempts to upload a file (such as images, audio, or documents) to the platform but the upload process encounters an error. Users see this message in a toast notification or error dialog when their file fails to upload due to network issues, file size limits, unsupported formats, or server errors.

component.description: A reusable file upload component that handles drag-and-drop or click-to-upload functionality across the platform. This component manages file validation, progress tracking, and error handling for various file types used in learning content creation.

upload_failed.usage: Error message displayed in a toast notification or inline error text when file upload fails
upload_failed.impact: High - Users need to understand when their content uploads fail so they can retry or troubleshoot the issue

invalid_type.context: This error message appears when a user attempts to upload a file that is not supported by the platform, such as when uploading media for learning units or assignments. The message displays immediately after file selection or during the upload process to inform users that their chosen file format cannot be processed.

component.description: File validation component that checks uploaded files against allowed formats and file size limits. It provides immediate feedback to users during the upload process and prevents unsupported files from being processed.

invalid_type.usage: Error message displayed in file upload dialogs or drag-and-drop areas after invalid file selection
invalid_type.impact: High - Critical for preventing user frustration and ensuring they understand why their upload failed so they can correct it

too_large.context: This error message appears when a user attempts to upload a file that exceeds the platform's maximum file size limit. It displays in file upload dialogs or drag-and-drop areas immediately after the user selects or drops an oversized file, preventing the upload from proceeding.

component.description: A reusable file upload component that handles media uploads for lesson content, assignment submissions, and profile images. It validates file size, type, and other constraints before initiating the upload process to AWS storage.

too_large.usage: Error message displayed in file upload validation feedback
too_large.impact: High - Users need clear feedback when uploads fail so they can take corrective action like compressing files or choosing smaller alternatives
